targets.text: govee-cli controls our Govee lamp from the CLI, an MCP server agents and the culture mesh can connect to, and a local web console with usage statistics
One govee_cli core module is the only code path to the lamp; CLI, MCP and web handlers all call it (no duplicated transport code)

Govee transport clients (cloud Developer API over HTTPS, LAN API over UDP 4001/4002/4003) built on stdlib urllib/socket/json, since pyproject.toml has dependencies = [] and CLAUDE.md forbids third-party runtime deps
pyproject.toml dependencies stays [] after the change; transports import only stdlib

New noun groups (devices, light, stats, mcp, serve) register via cli/__init__.py::_build_parser like _commands/cli.py, raise CliError with exit 2 for unreachable device/missing key, and update learn, overview _VERBS and explain catalog together for teken cli doctor --strict
teken cli doctor . --strict passes and every new verb has an explain catalog entry
Mutating verbs (on/off/brightness/color/temp/scene) dry-run unless --apply, in CLI and MCP alike; every verb has --json
Without --apply (CLI) / apply:true (MCP, web) no packet or HTTPS write leaves the host — asserted with a fake transport that records sends
API key is read from env (GOVEE_API_KEY), never committed; device IPs/MACs never in committed JSON; scripts/scan-secrets.py stays green
scripts/scan-secrets.py passes; GOVEE_API_KEY is only read from the environment
Statistics: every applied command and periodic state poll is logged to a local sqlite3 store under XDG state dir (outside git); web console charts usage from it
Stats DB path resolves under XDG_STATE_HOME (default ~/.local/state/govee-cli/), never inside the repo
Same-PR update of AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md, QWEN.md alongside CLAUDE.md; version bump
AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md, QWEN.md are updated in the same PR and pyproject version is bumped
Ori at home (CLI + phone browser on LAN/Tailscale) and AgentCulture agents — the govee-cli resident and any Claude-backed mesh agent — via MCP
Both audiences have a working entry point: a browser URL for Ori and an MCP tool list for agents
The repo is a template skeleton: no Govee code; the lamp is only controllable from the Govee Home phone app; agents cannot touch it; no usage history exists
git ls-files at 341ad19 contains no Govee transport code

'govee devices', 'govee light on|off|brightness|color|temp|scene --apply', 'govee stats', 'govee mcp serve' and 'govee serve' all drive the lamp through one core; the web console shows live state, controls and usage charts
Each listed verb exists in govee --help and has a test
Agents can make the lamp an ambient signal for the mesh (and Ori gets a faster console than the app), while dry-run defaults and a write log keep agent actions safe and auditable
Every applied write records source (cli/mcp/web) and actor in the event log
No third-party runtime deps; no Govee account login/password flow (API key only); no BLE transport; no committed key, IP or MAC
No BLE, no account-password login, no third-party runtime import anywhere in govee_cli/

Every web console endpoint (reads and writes) requires a bearer token generated on first 'govee serve' and stored 0600 in the XDG config dir; an unpaired browser gets only the pairing screen; pairing hardening per c32
Write endpoint returns 401 without a valid token; token file mode is 0600

Stats views: on-time per day (bar), brightness/color-temp over time (line), commands by source cli/mcp/web/agent (bar), last-24h state timeline; data from sqlite events + state samples taken by 'govee serve' every 60s
Each of the four charts renders from real sqlite rows, with an empty state when there is no data
From a phone on the LAN, toggling the lamp in the web console changes the physical lamp in < 2 s over LAN, and the action appears in stats within 60 s
Measured in a manual LAN test on the real lamp after the build
A Claude agent with only .mcp.json can list devices and turn the lamp on in 2 tool calls (dry-run then apply); 100% of applied writes from cli/mcp/web land in the event log
MCP integration test drives tools/list + tools/call over stdio against a fake transport
uv run pytest -n auto passes with coverage >= 60% using fake LAN/cloud transports (no lamp needed in CI); teken cli doctor --strict and scan-secrets stay green
CI run on the PR shows pytest, lint, teken doctor and scan-secrets green

govee-cli ships a culture-rules 'runner' actor definition (docs/culture-rules/govee-actor.json) registering argv commands lamp_on, lamp_off, lamp_brightness {pct}, lamp_color {hex}, lamp_temp {kelvin}, lamp_scene {name}, each 'govee light ... --apply --json'; it is imported with 'culture-rules actors import' (dry run unless --apply) by the user, not by govee-cli
The definition passes 'culture-rules actors create --json' dry run (the user runs it with their CULTURE_RULES_TOKEN); no argv entry is a shell/interpreter (inline_guard would refuse it)

Web console: the custom color picker previews the color on the lamp visual while it is still open (before selection); the color is committed or sent only on pick. Showing or hiding the dry-run preview note must not move the lamp visual (user feedback on prototype v1, 2026-10-29)

A Playwright check of the real console: dispatching 'input' on the custom color picker changes the lamp visual's color without sending a command, 'change' commits it, and the bulb's bounding box is identical with the preview note shown and hidden

One LAN listener per host: Govee devices reply to UDP 4002 regardless of source port, so while 'govee serve' runs, the CLI and MCP server send LAN reads/writes through serve's loopback API; without serve they bind 4002 themselves, and a busy port exits 2 with 'port 4002 is in use (govee serve or another Govee integration)'
With a fake serve holding 4002, a CLI LAN call goes through the loopback API; with 4002 held by a foreign socket and no serve, the CLI exits 2 with the port-in-use message

LAN writes are UDP with no acknowledgement, so an applied write is logged 'sent', then verified by a devStatus read within 3 s and updated to 'confirmed' or 'unconfirmed'; stats and the activity feed show the difference
A fake LAN device that drops the packet yields an event logged 'unconfirmed'; one that applies it yields 'confirmed'

LAN multicast is pinned to an interface (GOVEE_LAN_INTERFACE or --interface, default: the interface of the default route); 'govee doctor' reports the interface used, whether discovery got any reply, and the remediation list (enable LAN Control in Govee Home, allow inbound UDP 4002, pick another interface)
govee doctor --json lists the interface used and a lan-discovery check with remediation when no device replies

Web console token hardening: the pairing link carries the token in the URL fragment (#token=, never sent to the server or logged); the page moves it to localStorage and clears the hash; writes need the Authorization header (no cookie, so no CSRF) and a same-origin Origin header; comparison uses hmac.compare_digest; 'govee serve --rotate-token' invalidates every paired device; request bodies capped at 16 KiB
The four web tests (401 no token, 403 wrong Origin, 401 after rotate, 413 oversize) pass; server access log never contains the token
Stats store opens sqlite in WAL mode with busy_timeout 5000 ms because serve's poller, the CLI and the MCP server write concurrently; a schema_version table makes later migrations explicit
Two processes writing events concurrently for 5 s produce no 'database is locked' error; PRAGMA journal_mode returns wal

The culture-rules runner actor definition pins machine: spark (the host on the lamp's LAN) and uses the absolute path to the govee binary, because runner commands start with a minimal environment (culture_rules/actors/code.py docstring); LAN verbs need no key, and the scene command documents that GOVEE_API_KEY must be injected via grant or it exits 2
The actor JSON has machine 'spark', every argv[0] is absolute, and no argv is a shell or interpreter

Cloud usage stays far under the Developer API's daily cap (10,000 requests/key/day per community docs, unverified officially): state polling uses LAN; when only cloud is available serve polls every 5 min at most; HTTP 429 exits 2 with the reset time from the response headers
A fake cloud returning 429 with reset headers makes the CLI exit 2 and print the reset time; serve's cloud-only poll interval is >= 300 s

docs ship a systemd --user unit for 'govee serve' (restart on failure, EnvironmentFile for GOVEE_API_KEY outside the repo), since stats sampling only happens while serve runs; stats show gaps where serve was down instead of interpolating
systemd-analyze verify passes on the shipped unit; a stats chart over a serve outage shows a gap, not 'off'

The CLI rolls new tokens so agents can pair apps and MCP servers locally: 'govee token new --name <label>' mints a named token (printed once, plus a #token= pairing link), 'govee token list' shows names/created/last-used (never the secret), 'govee token revoke <name>' removes one; 'govee serve --rotate-token' still revokes all. Tokens are stored hashed in a 0600 file under the XDG config dir; the MCP server and CLI use a token (GOVEE_TOKEN or their own minted one) when routing through serve's loopback API (user requirement, 2026-10-29)

A token minted with 'govee token new' authenticates against serve's API, appears by name in 'token list' without its secret, and returns 401 immediately after 'token revoke'; the token file holds only hashes and has mode 0600

tasks.summary: Core types and a recording fake transport
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/govee/types.py defines frozen dataclasses Device, LampState, Command (verb, transport, payload) and a Transport Protocol (discover, get_state, send); kelvin_to_rgb(2000..9000) is tested at 2000/6500/9000
govee_cli/govee/fake.py FakeTransport records every send() and can be told to drop packets or return a scripted state; tests/test_govee_types.py passes
only stdlib imports
tasks.instruction: Create the govee_cli/govee/ package. Keep the Transport Protocol minimal; LAN and cloud transports (t5, t6) and LampService (t7) build on it. No CLI wiring here.

tasks.summary: Stats store: sqlite in WAL with events, samples and chart queries
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/stats/store.py db_path() resolves under XDG_STATE_HOME, default ~/.local/state/govee-cli/stats.db, never inside the repo
every connection sets journal_mode=WAL and busy_timeout=5000 and creates a schema_version table; two processes writing for 5 s raise no 'database is locked'

tables events(ts, source cli|mcp|web|rules, actor, verb, payload, status dry_run|sent|confirmed|unconfirmed) and samples(ts, on, brightness, rgb, kelvin); query functions return hours-on per day, commands per day by source, 24h samples with gaps where no sample exists for > 3 min, and weekday x hour minutes-on
tasks.instruction: Stdlib sqlite3 only. tests/test_stats_store.py uses tmp_path and monkeypatched XDG_STATE_HOME. Gaps are data, never interpolated as 'off' (c36).

custom color input previews on the lamp visual without a request; change commits; the bulb's bounding box is identical with the preview note shown and hidden

No CDN except Google Fonts Albert Sans with system fallback. Static files must ship in the wheel (they live under govee_cli/).

Document in docs/culture-rules/README.md how the user imports it (culture-rules actors import, dry run then --apply) and one example rule: CI failed -> lamp_color FF0000. No schedules in govee-cli.

tasks.summary: LAN transport: discovery, control and status over UDP
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/govee/lan.py implements Transport: scan multicasts {cmd:scan} to 239.255.255.250:4001 on the interface from GOVEE_LAN_INTERFACE / argument / default-route interface (IP_MULTICAST_IF), listens on 4002; send() emits turn/brightness/colorwc JSON to device:4003; get_state() sends devStatus and waits for the 4002 reply
binding 4002 when it is held raises a typed PortBusy error carrying the port-in-use message; tests use injected sockets / a fake device on 127.0.0.1 and never real multicast
only stdlib imports (socket, json, select)
tasks.instruction: devStatus target port is an open risk (4003 vs 4002): make it a module constant with a comment pointing at the plan risk, defaulting to 4003.

tasks.summary: Cloud transport: Govee Developer API over urllib
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/govee/cloud.py implements Transport plus scenes(device) and set_scene(); the key comes only from os.environ['GOVEE_API_KEY'] and is never logged, echoed or put in an error message
HTTP 429 raises a typed RateLimited error with the reset time parsed from response headers; missing key raises a typed MissingKey error; tests run against a local http.server fake, never the real API
the base URL lives in Python source (not committed JSON) so scan-secrets stays green
tasks.instruction: Check developer.govee.com for the current endpoint family (router/api/v1 device/control with capability objects vs the older v1 appliance API) before coding; see plan risk. urllib.request only.

tasks.summary: LampService: one code path, dry run by default, verified writes, logged
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/govee/service.py LampService.apply(change, *, apply=False, source, actor) returns the planned Command list; with apply=False no Transport.send is called (FakeTransport proves it); with apply=True exactly the previewed commands are sent

LAN first, cloud fallback per command (scenes always cloud); an applied LAN write is logged 'sent' then verified with get_state within 3 s and updated to 'confirmed' or 'unconfirmed'; dry runs are logged 'dry_run'; every event carries source and actor

when a serve loopback endpoint is reachable (GOVEE_SERVE_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:<port>) with a token, LAN operations route through it; otherwise LAN is used directly and PortBusy maps to CliError exit 2 with the port-in-use message
tasks.instruction: This is the only module that touches transports; CLI, MCP and web call LampService. Missing key / unreachable device / rate limit map to CliError(2, ..., remediation).

tasks.summary: CLI verbs: devices, light, stats, token, serve and mcp entry points, doctor LAN checks
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/cli/_commands/{devices,light,stats,token,serve,mcp}.py register via _build_parser; light on|off|brightness|color|temp|scene print the planned command and exit 0 without --apply, send with --apply; every verb supports --json and keeps the stdout/stderr split
serve and 'mcp serve' import govee_cli.web.server.run / govee_cli.mcp.server.run lazily; token new|list|revoke call govee_cli.auth.tokens
doctor adds checks lan-interface, lan-discovery (with remediation: enable LAN Control, allow inbound UDP 4002, set GOVEE_LAN_INTERFACE), api-key-present (never printing the key), stats-db-writable

learn (text + JSON), overview _VERBS, explain/catalog.py entries and the template strings named in CLAUDE.md (parser description, learn._TEXT, catalog._ROOT, overview._ARTIFACTS) describe govee-cli; teken cli doctor . --strict passes; tests/test_cli_light.py etc. pass
tasks.instruction: This task owns govee_cli/cli/** and govee_cli/explain/** only, so t9/t10/t11 stay file-disjoint. Use parser_class=type(p) for nested subparsers as _commands/cli.py does. source='cli', actor = $USER.

tasks.summary: MCP server: stdio JSON-RPC with lamp tools
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/mcp/server.py run() speaks MCP over stdio (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, ping) with tools list_devices, get_state, set_light, set_scene, get_stats; set_* default to dry run and only send with apply: true
every call logs source=mcp and actor from GOVEE_ACTOR, else the initialize clientInfo name; errors return MCP tool errors carrying the CliError message and remediation, never a traceback
tests/test_mcp_server.py drives the server over a subprocess pipe against FakeTransport: two calls (dry run, then apply) turn the lamp on
tasks.instruction: Stdlib json + sys.stdin/stdout line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0. Target MCP protocol version 2025-06-18. Never read GOVEE_API_KEY here; LampService owns transports.

tasks.summary: Web server: token-gated API, static console, loopback LAN owner
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/web/server.py run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8742) serves govee_cli/web/static and /api/{state,light,scene,stats,events,lan}; every /api route requires a valid bearer token (401 otherwise), including reads

writes also require a same-origin Origin header (403 otherwise); bodies over 16 KiB get 413; tokens never appear in the access log; --rotate-token revokes all tokens and prints a fresh pairing link with the token in the #fragment
/api/lan is the loopback-only LAN proxy LampService uses while serve owns UDP 4002 (refuses non-loopback clients); tests/test_web_server.py covers 401, 403, 413, rotate, loopback-only
tasks.instruction: http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer, stdlib only. Owns govee_cli/web/server.py only (static files are t3, poller is t11). source='web', actor = token name.

tasks.summary: State poller: 60 s LAN samples, 5 min cloud-only, gaps not zeros
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/web/poller.py samples lamp state every 60 s over LAN, or every 300 s when only cloud is available, writing samples rows; a RateLimited error backs off until the reset time
a stopped poller leaves no rows, so the stats queries report a gap instead of 'off'; tests/test_poller.py uses a fake clock and FakeTransport
tasks.instruction: Runs as a daemon thread started by web.server.run(); exposes start()/stop(). No schedules or time-of-day logic beyond the sampling interval.

tasks.summary: Live acceptance on the real lamp
acceptance_criteria: with LAN Control enabled, govee devices finds the lamp; a web console toggle from a phone changes it in < 2 s and the event appears in stats within 60 s; results recorded in docs/live-test-results/ with date and model
devStatus target port verified and the lan.py constant updated if needed; an applied write shows 'confirmed'
the user runs 'culture-rules actors create --json' as a dry run with docs/culture-rules/govee-actor.json and it validates
the main agent's own live run is recorded in docs/live-test-results/ before the user's run is requested
tasks.instruction: The main agent live-tests first, before the user: from spark it runs govee devices / light commands against the real lamp over LAN (and cloud if GOVEE_API_KEY is set), drives the web console with Playwright at phone width, verifies the devStatus port, and records measured results in docs/live-test-results/. Only then does the user repeat the phone toggle and run the culture-rules dry-run import with CULTURE_RULES_TOKEN. Record measured numbers only; a failure is recorded as a failure.

tasks.summary: Token store: named, hashed, revocable pairing tokens
acceptance_criteria: govee_cli/auth/tokens.py: new(name) returns a 32-byte urlsafe secret once and stores only its sha256 with name, created, last_used in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/govee-cli/tokens.json at mode 0600; list() never returns secrets; revoke(name); revoke_all(); verify(secret) uses hmac.compare_digest and updates last_used
duplicate names are refused; a revoked token fails verify() immediately; tests/test_tokens.py checks file mode and that the file contains no secret
tasks.instruction: Stdlib only (secrets, hashlib, hmac, json, os). Atomic writes (temp file + os.replace) so concurrent CLI and serve processes never read a half-written file.

risks.text: devStatus query target port (4003 vs 4002) unverified until the real lamp answers

Govee cloud endpoint family CONFIRMED by t6 from developer.govee.com (openapi.api.govee.com/router/api/v1: user/devices, device/state, device/control, device/scenes with capability objects). Still unverified: rate-limit header names and limits (docs silent; cloud.py accepts Retry-After, API-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Reset), colorTemperatureK readback, and the control success shape (code == 200). Verify in t14 with a real key.

Lamp is a Govee H6076A floor lamp (RGBIC; A variant also supports Matter); H6076 reported LAN-capable by third-party drivers. No LAN reply to multicast or unicast scans on 192.168.1.0/24 (wlP9s9). Firewall ruled out: ufw is inactive (user ran 'ufw status'); a UDP 4002 allow rule was added anyway. Remaining causes: LAN Control toggle off / not offered on this firmware, or the lamp not on this subnet. t14 cannot pass until the lamp answers.
